description: Impact between a vessel and another vessel while both are underway or maneuvering.
Vessel makes unintended contact with the seabed, shore, or underwater obstruction and becomes grounded or stranded.
Impact between a vessel and a fixed or floating object other than another vessel (for example, wharf, buoy, bridge, or moored structure).
Onboard fire, combustion event, or explosion involving cargo, fuel, machinery, or accommodation spaces.
Failure of propulsion or essential mechanical systems (for example, main engine, gearbox, shafting, or steering machinery).
Failure of onboard equipment not primarily propulsion machinery (for example, navigation, communications, safety, or deck equipment).
Vessel develops severe heel/list or overturns, affecting stability and survivability.
Structural breach of hull or failure of watertight integrity (doors, hatches, seals) allowing uncontrolled water ingress.
An occurrence where one or more persons die as a result of marine operations or onboard events.
A marine occurrence resulting in major injury requiring significant medical treatment or hospitalization.
Physical damage to the vessel or onboard systems/equipment without necessarily involving total loss. Losing equipment (i.e containers lost overboard) should be included here.
Uncontrolled ingress of water into the vessel, compartments, or critical spaces.
Unsafe proximity between vessels with elevated collision risk requiring immediate avoiding action.
Person(s) or vessel unaccounted for and presumed lost after search or elapsed time.
Release or discharge of pollutants (for example, oil, fuel, chemicals, or cargo contaminants) into the marine environment.
Marine occurrence that does not fit any other listed category.
Vessel sinks or is overwhelmed by water and lost from buoyancy/stability failure.
Occurrence involving launch, recovery, operation, or failure of lifeboats or rescue craft.
Failure, malfunction, or damage involving aircraft structural components (fuselage, wings, control surfaces, landing gear).
Event involving engine or propulsion system performance, failure, or shutdown.
Failure or malfunction of aircraft onboard systems (electrical, hydraulic, pneumatic, avionics, etc.).
Loss or reduction of required separation between aircraft in flight or on maneuvering areas.
Unauthorized or incorrect entry into controlled/restricted/prohibited airspace.
Error by air navigation service personnel (i.e ATC) affecting traffic management, loss of separation or clearances.
Breach of operational procedures, rules, SOPs, or approved limitations.
Failure of coordination between flight crew, ATC units, operators, or other parties.
Airspace-related occurrence not captured by the other specific airspace categories.
Aircraft encounter or conflict with a drone/RPAS posing collision or distraction risk.
Air traffic management process/event affecting traffic flow, sequencing, control, or safety margins.
Issue with navigation aids (for example, ILS, VOR, NDB, GNSS augmentation) affecting navigation guidance.
Failure or degradation of surveillance systems (radar, ADS-B, multilateration) used for separation/control.
Failure, degradation, or misuse of runway or approach lighting systems affecting operations.
Aerodrome or supporting infrastructure issue not covered by specific infrastructure categories.
Ground-based interference affecting aircraft safety (for example, laser illumination, projectile strike, unauthorized signals).
Adverse meteorological conditions materially contributing to the occurrence.
Bird/wildlife strike or wildlife presence creating risk during flight or ground operations.
Environmental factor other than weather/wildlife (for example, smoke, ash, contaminants) affecting safe operation.
Intentional forced landing on water.
Diversion to alternate aerodrome or return to departure due to safety/technical/operational reasons.
Emergency disembarkation/evacuation using normal or emergency exits.
Unplanned descent initiated for immediate safety reasons.
Landing made as a result of actual or suspected abnormal condition requiring prompt landing.
Intentional fuel jettison or holding to reduce landing weight for operational/safety reasons.
Discontinued approach or rejected landing with climb away from runway environment.
Take-off roll intentionally aborted before liftoff.
Consequence-event category for operational outcomes not covered elsewhere.
Loss, degradation, or anomaly in control of aircraft attitude, flight path, or handling.
Weight, balance, or loading configuration issue affecting performance or controllability.
Communication failure, misunderstanding, or loss affecting safe operation.
Occurrence involving crew/cabin safety procedures, injury risk, or cabin operations.
Presence of fire, smoke, or fumes in or around the aircraft impacting safety.
Pre-flight planning or navigation execution issue contributing to the event.

Fuel quantity, quality, management, contamination, or supply issue affecting operations. Fuel starvation which cause other events (such as dithcings, forced landings, Terrain collisions etc.) should be included in their respective categories.
Occurrence during taxi, pushback, towing, ramp, or apron activities.
Triggered terrain/obstacle proximity alerts or warnings indicating reduced terrain clearance margin.
Aviation occurrence not fitting any other listed category.
Runway-related occurrence (for example, excursion, incursion, confusion, unstable landing outcome).
Collision or impact with terrain, obstacles, or water due to inadequate clearance.
Occurrence where alcohol or drug use/impairment concerns are relevant to rail safety.
Impact involving train-to-train, train-to-vehicle, or train-to-object collisions. Use level crossing category for collisions at crossings.
Failure or degradation of communications systems critical to safe rail operations.
Occurrence involving hazardous materials release, exposure, handling issue, or associated risk.
Wheelset leaves the rails, partially or fully, during movement or operations.
Fault or anomaly in traction power or electrical infrastructure affecting operations.
Detonation or rapid overpressure event causing safety consequences in rail context.
Combustion event affecting rolling stock, infrastructure, cargo, or surrounding areas.
Occurrence involving gas leak, ignition, exposure, or gas-related hazard.
Occurrence at a road-rail or pedestrian-rail crossing interface. Any collision at a crossing should be categorized as a level crossing occurrence, not a collision.

Value: Light Rail or Tram Authority Exceeded
description: Light rail/tram movement proceeds beyond authorized limits or permissions.
Unsafe, shifted, insecure, overweight, or otherwise irregular load affecting rail safety.
Rail occurrence that does not fit any other listed category.
Train movement exceeds the limits of movement authority.
Security-related occurrence affecting rail network safety or operations.
Defect or irregular condition in locomotives, wagons, carriages, or other rolling stock.
Uncontrolled rail vehicle movement without intended braking/control.
Non-compliance with safeworking rules or procedural protections. This should be used if it caused or nearly caused an occurrence.

Value: Signalling And Other Proceed Authority System Irregularities
description: Irregularity in signaling or movement-authority systems used to protect train movements.
Train passes a stop signal without authority.
Person sustains or risks injury due to slipping, tripping, or falling in rail environment.
Defect or irregularity in track, structures, or civil assets affecting safety.

Value: Train Warning and Enforcement System Irregularity
description: Issue with onboard/trackside warning or enforcement systems (for example, ATP/TPWS-like protections).
Unauthorized person on rail corridor, track, or restricted rail property causing safety risk.
Safety-critical failure that presents a less restrictive/unsafe indication than intended.
